note.question: How do endogenous evaluation and sequential search interact?
note.overview: When consumers evaluate product value under sequential search, higher sampling costs may in equilibrium lead to more sampling, lower prices and profits, and greater consumer surplus.

components.formal: Objective relation: This captures the intuition that a higher search cost can soften price competition by demotivating consumer search.
conditions: Suppose evaluation is costless such that the consumers can perfectly be informed of the value of each searched product.

Moreover, we adopt the conventional assumption that, in case a consumer observes that a firm charges an off-equilibrium price, his or her equilibrium belief about the to-be-sampled products’ prices remains unchanged.

The consumer then decides whether to make a purchase (among the sampled products) or to continue the search process and sample another product (and, conditional on search, sets the level of evaluation effort for the nextsampled product).
